This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Giles Snyder.
Democrats have delivered a massive blow to President Trump
and the Republican Party sweeping to victory
in the midterm elections.
The party has split both the House and Senate,
dramatically changing the balance of power in Washington.
NPR's Windsor Johnston has more on some of the night's biggest upsets.
Well, Democrats have picked up seven seats in the Senate,
including Maine, where long-time Republican Senator
Susan Collins lost her bid for a sixth term to Democrat Troy Jackson.
If you're watching this after getting home from a shift
or sitting at the table, wondering how you're going to pay the next bill,
I want you to hear something very clearly.
You are sending somebody to Washington who knows exactly what that feels like.
Democrats have taken control of the House, flipping at least 25 Republican-held seats,
among them Indiana's fifth congressional district,
where Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican Victoria Sparks.
Oh my gosh, friends.
The amount of doors that you knocked in the blazing hot sun.
The amount of phone calls that you made.
The amount of handwritten postcards that you sent.
This win is because of you.
Democrats also flipped House seats in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and North Carolina,
helping the party reclaim its majority.
The new Congress will take office in January,
setting up a divided government that could make it much harder
for President Trump to advance his legislative agenda.
Democratic Socialist Milak Keros was the winner of
Colorado's first congressional district, Emma Banda 90, member station KUNC reports.
Keros is the first Gen Z member of Congress.
She's also the first black woman Colorado has elected representative.
She acknowledged how new she was to the position
as she took the stage at the Democratic Watch Party in Denver late Tuesday night.
I'm going to learn a lot from the people in this delegation
who've been in these buildings longer than I have.
And I plan to ask a lot of questions.
But I'm also going to stay true to what Denver sent me to do.
Keros highlighted the need for more affordable housing, criticized high energy bills,
and emphasized treating health care as a basic human right.
Keros also thanked former incumbent Diana DeGette for serving Denver for 30 years.
For NPR News, I'm Emma Banda 90 in Denver, Colorado.
President Trump spoke to Fox News overnight saying Democrats, in his words,
did a good job in their campaigns and blaming Republican candidates for the party's losses.
He said he would work with Democrats on issues such as immigration,
though he threatened to veto what he called any insane bill they passed.
This is NPR.
The Trump administration has apparently canceled a flight deporting Afghan nationals seeking
protection in the U.S. NPR's Quill Lawrence reports many of them aided or fought alongside U.S. troops.
66 members of Congress signed a letter to the secretaries of state and homeland security
to halt deportation flights of Iranians or Afghans to their home country or to Pakistan.
The letter said 150 Afghan nationals were slated for deportation,
some of whom had fled Afghanistan because they helped the U.S. mission there.
A coalition called Afghan EVAC announced the flight has now been canceled
at a press conference where Sarah Mehta with the ACLU spoke.
We're certainly relieved to see a respite today to know that vulnerable Afghan allies
are not going to be deported today to Afghanistan where some of them faced potentially death.
The State Department referred questions to DHS,
which referred questions to ICE, which did not respond by airtime.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
An inmate who escaped from a Tennessee prison has been recaptured.
Authorities say Jacob Morley was apprehended Tuesday near Kansas City
with troopers using roadside cameras and a helicopter to track him down.
Morley escaped from Tennessee's northwest correctional complex more than a week ago.
Federal safety investigators have confirmed that the business jet
that crashed in South Florida Sunday afternoon was breaking apart before it came down.
The National Transportation Safety Board says three pieces of the jet have been found between
1.3 and 3.8 miles away from the main crash site.
The plane crashed into a residential area near West Palm Beach.
Nine people on board were killed.
I'm Jael Snyder. This is NPR News.

topics.text: Democrats win control of the House and reshape the balance of power in Washington
Democrat Troy Jackson defeats Republican Senator Susan Collins in Maine
Democrats flip at least 25 House seats, including J.D. Ford's win in Indiana's fifth district
Democrat Millie Keros wins Colorado's first district, becoming the first Gen Z member of Congress
Trump tells Fox News Democrats ran good campaigns and blames Republican candidates for losses
Trump administration cancels deportation flight carrying Afghan nationals who aided U.S. troops
Escaped Tennessee inmate Jacob Morley recaptured near Kansas City after more than a week
